The 15 new bytes[]/string[] inits still peel one 'mem[p + 32] = 96' before 'while idx - 1:' (a one-statement rotation, within the new two-statement limit).

regressions.source: Governor.sol execute/cancel: hashProposal(...) then state(proposalId) (require ... 'Governor: proposal not successful' / 'not active'), quorum -> getPastTotalSupply, _cancel -> _timelock.cancel(_timelockIds[proposalId]); propose: getVotes(msg.sender, block.number - 1) after _storeProposal's hashProposal
regressions.issue: Everything after the inlined hashProposal encode loops is now addressed from an unknown mem[64]. The write 'mem[64] = t' (t is the loop's exit value) is not forwarded to later reads, and '_N = mem[64]' is not identified with mem[64]. Result in these 7 functions: 34 string reverts became raw memory; getPastTotalSupply, getPastVotes, isOperationDone and the state-changing timelock.cancel lost names and arguments (P2 +34 lines); mapping keys became concat(mem[0]) (P4 +19) or raw stor[sha3(mem[0 len 64]) + 1]; 9 events print id=mem[mem[64]]; the guard 'if s != 4: revert' became an if/else nest; a dominated 'Checkpoints: block not yet mined' check and dead mem[0]/mem[32] writes reappear. Functions grew by 50-80 lines each.
regressions.rule: A write 'mem[64] = e', for any expression e including a loop's exit value, gives every later read of mem[64] the value e until the next write to mem[64]. A variable assigned mem[64] equals mem[64] until then, so '_N - mem[64]' is 0. Apply this before matching Error(string) reverts, ABI call arguments, mapping keys written through mem[0], and event data.
regressions.verified: text_check run --per-selector 16 on the new text: 0 different in 787+787 calls, so the text is still exact; the regression is readability (compare old 2073-2110 with new 1890-1940)

regressions.source: Governor.sol hashProposal: return uint256(keccak256(abi.encode(targets, values, calldatas, descriptionHash)))
regressions.issue: Same cause on a small scale: the offset words of the encoding keep '_8 - mem[64]', and the return reads mem[64] right after 'mem[64] = t'.
regressions.rule: As above: forward 'mem[64] = t' to the reads after it and fold '_N - mem[64]' to 0 while no write to mem[64] intervenes.

improvements: castVoteBySig 380 -> 145 lines (ECDSA reverts as strings, getPastVotes named, P2 -6). state, proposals and the castVote family lose their dead memory and mapping-scratch writes (138 -> 87, 217 -> 157, 161 -> 106 lines), isOperationPending is named in 6 functions, 'if not s: x = 0 else: ...' became 's and ...', and the always-reverting arm of castVote* is flattened. relay's error-message revert is now a string. VoteCast/VoteCastWithParams decoded. onlyGovernance loops fixed (finding 1).
notes: Reviewed by structure (5617-line diff, 24 functions changed, 1 display-only; several functions only moved in the text: compared by body). Calls, logs and storage writes per function unchanged; the 2 removed string reverts in castVote* merged with an identical revert at the end of their arm. P2 23 -> 45 and P4 23 -> 42 come entirely from regression 1 (P2 -12 elsewhere).
summary: Regression (medium): in the 7 functions that inline hashProposal's encode loop, the free-memory pointer is lost after the loop, so reverts, the getPastTotalSupply/getPastVotes/isOperationDone/timelock.cancel calls, mapping keys and ProposalExecuted/Canceled events print as raw memory. Elsewhere the text improved: castVoteBySig, state, proposals and castVote* are much shorter, VoteCast events are decoded and the onlyGovernance loop is a clean do-while.
